_comment: Narration for the demo video, one cue per scene.
`at` is the cue's start in seconds and must sit inside its scene's window,
which is set by the scene durations in src/PrahariDemo.tsx. If you retime a
scene there, retime the cue here — scripts/voiceover.py checks every cue
against `scene_start`/`scene_end` and refuses to build a track that drifts.
Lines are written to be spoken, not read: short sentences, no acronyms the
synthesiser would spell out ('SIF', 'HSE', 'NLP'), and no numbers written as
digits where a word reads better. They track the on-screen captions closely
so the voice never contradicts the text under it.

cues.text: Potential is not severity. Prahari finds the incidents that could have killed someone.
Safety systems rank what happened. The fatal ones give warning first.
Seven hundred field reports, ranked by what could have happened. A hundred and twenty carry fatal energy with no barrier. Measured, not claimed.
A slip in the canteen. A bruised knee. Every system tracks this one, and prahari ranks it low.
Now a relief valve, deliberately bypassed. The flange blew out. Nobody was hurt, so anywhere else this closes today. Prahari escalates it.
Hybrid, but not a black box. The model only extracts facts. Named rules decide. Same text, same verdict, every time.
Nine named rules fired. Each one cites a published standard, and the exact characters that triggered it. Auditable, without trusting the model.
Field reports are not written in clean English. This one is Hinglish, and the engine still finds eighteen spans of evidence.
One report is noise. The same barrier failing at the same site is a pattern. At Moran, it failed six times.
The accumulation index rises when the same barrier keeps failing in the same place. That is a number a safety meeting can fund.
Every term the engine reasons with is published, and served from the engine itself.
Every verdict traces to a named rule, and the exact characters that fired it. And it runs completely offline.
